paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus asks, "Who do you say I am?" (Mark 8:29), and that question is for YOU, not just for Peter. Passing along what everybody else says is easy. Peter answered, "You are the Christ," and that is the answer the whole passage stands on.

But look at what comes next. Jesus says the Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, be killed and rise again after three days (Mark 8:31). Peter didn't like that plan, and Jesus told him, "you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men" (Mark 8:33). I think we all have a little Peter in us, friend. We want the crown without the cross, and I have NO room to talk.

So Jesus tells the crowd what following Him costs: "he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me" (Mark 8:34). Hold your life tight and you lose it, but lose it for His sake and for the gospel and you save it (Mark 8:35). "What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?" (Mark 8:36). Nothing, baker, NOTHING. Jesus is worth more than all of it, so don't be ashamed of Him or His words (Mark 8:38).
